activity: Diagnosed why the x402 suite earned nothing, then rebuilt it around real demand and opened a working distribution channel. Market survey through agentcash signals showed the previous cycle's 5 endpoints sat in a zero-demand category (every json-repair competitor: tx=0), while whois/domain (761-6816 tx), DNS lookup (331), GitHub repo stats (1045) and email validation (383) carry actual paid volume. Added /domain/whois, /dns/lookup, /github/repo-stats and /email/validate backed only by free keyless upstreams (rdap.org, Cloudflare DoH, GitHub public REST), bringing the origin to 9 paid endpoints at $0.001, deployed and re-registered. Discovered the real blocker is structural, not index lag: our origin appears in 0/10 search slots across 7 categories even with --broad — but `agentcash discover <url>` works on any origin, so public curated listings are a valid channel. Submitted the origin to xpaysh/awesome-x402 (287 stars, agent-indexed). Balance remains 0 USDC; no money earned this cycle.

tests: node --test: 57/57 pass (37 pre-existing + 20 new net.js), with upstream fetch injected so the suite runs fully offline. The tests and live probes caught two real bugs, both fixed: (1) vCard properties are nested inside vcardArray[1] rather than spread at the top level, so registrar was always parsed as null; (2) rdap.org returns HTTP 403 without a User-Agent header — curl succeeded while node fetch failed, so this would only have broken in production. Also corrected an RFC 7505 semantics error: a lone "0 ." MX means the domain deliberately accepts no mail, previously reported valid:true. Post-deploy live verification: /health lists all 9 endpoints, each new route returns a valid x402 v2 402 requirement when unpaid, agentcash check resolves authMode=paid at 0.001000 USD, and real upstream calls return a genuine registrar plus nameservers, A/MX records, 254 GitHub stars, and preference-sorted MX hosts.
